title: DOW-UAP-D081, Narrative Statement 3, Western United States Event, 2023
what_is_it: First-hand witness narrative memorandum submitted to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) describing UAP sightings by a federal law enforcement special agent.
core_summary: Witness 3, a U.S. federal law enforcement special agent, describes two UAP encounters over two consecutive nights in mid-October 2023 in the western United States. The first event involved a large orange orb that alternated between orange and clear, moved rapidly across the sky, and expelled three smaller red orbs in what appeared to be a mechanical action. The second event involved four red lights that hovered in a square formation over an airfield, orange orbs near a ridgeline, and a mysterious vehicle on the ground that flashed its headlights methodically and evaded pursuit by apparently floating off-road across rough terrain without leaving tire tracks.
interpretation_warnings: Single-source witness account: this is one person's recollection; no corroborating sensor data, photographs, or radar tracks are included in this document.
Witness 3 was one of several agents who reported sightings, but no other witness statements are included here for cross-reference.
Distances, sizes, and speeds are all subjective estimates — the witness explicitly noted inability to determine how far away or how large the objects were.
Observations were made at dusk and near-darkness; the second event relied on night vision goggles, which can affect perception of colour, size, and distance.

The narrative was provided as a free-form recollection to AARO, not a structured debrief, and the witness notes uncertainty on several details (e.g., 'I don't recall if the orange orbs released red orbs').
The document is dated June 2026, roughly 2.5 years after the October 2023 events, introducing potential memory degradation.
The specific location within the western United States is not disclosed, nor is the airfield identified.

public_headline: Federal Agent Reports Orange Orbs and Evasive Vehicle in Western US
public_tldr: A U.S. federal law enforcement special agent submitted a first-hand account to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) describing two UAP encounters over consecutive nights in October 2023 in the western United States. The sightings included a colour-shifting orange orb that expelled smaller red orbs, red lights hovering in formation over an airfield, and a ground vehicle that evaded pursuit by apparently floating off-road without leaving tracks.
public_narrative:
This document is a witness narrative memorandum submitted to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), the Pentagon body responsible for investigating unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP). It was signed by AARO Director Jon T. Kosloski and dated 02 June 2026, roughly two and a half years after the events it describes.

The witness, identified only as "Witness 3," is a U.S. federal law enforcement special agent who was one of several agents reporting UAP sightings over two days in mid-October 2023 in the western United States. The specific location is not disclosed.

During the first event, at approximately 7 p.m. at dusk, the witness observed a large orange orb that alternated between orange and clear every two to three seconds. It moved roughly 20 degrees across the sky in three to five seconds, then expelled three smaller red orbs in what the witness described as a mechanical action. The red orbs moved south in a straight line. No sound or exhaust trails were observed. The entire event lasted about 30 to 45 seconds.

The second event occurred either the same night or the following night, between 8 and 8:30 p.m. Using night vision goggles, the witness saw four red lights travel from north to south, covering about 90 degrees in five to ten seconds, then stop and hover in a square formation over the four corners of an airfield. Orange orbs were also seen near a ridgeline. On the ground, an unidentified vehicle flashed its headlights at a regular tempo. When the witnesses attempted to approach, the vehicle maintained a distance of roughly 100 yards and then appeared to float off-road across rough terrain. A later search found no tire tracks. When the vehicle disappeared, the aerial objects were gone as well. This event lasted about two to three minutes.

The document does not include any agency conclusion about what was observed. No sensor data, photographs, or radar tracks accompany the narrative. AARO has not attributed the sightings to any specific origin in this document.
public_caveats: This is a single-source witness account with no corroborating sensor data, photographs, or radar tracks included in the document.
All distances, sizes, and speeds are the witness's subjective estimates — the witness explicitly noted an inability to judge how far away or how large the objects were.
The account was written roughly 2.5 years after the events (document dated June 2026, events in October 2023), which introduces potential memory degradation.
Observations during the second event were made in near-darkness using night vision goggles, which can distort colour, size, and distance perception.
Other agents also reported sightings, but their statements are not included here for cross-reference, and no agency conclusions or explanations are provided.
